fields.title: gh refuses to print a failing CI job's log
symptom-keywords: logs will be available when it is complete

sections.Symptom:
You want the `##[error]` line behind a red check on a pull request, and `gh` prints no log.

`gh run view --job <job-id> --log-failed` refuses while any other job in the run is still going:

```text
run is still in progress; logs will be available when it is complete
```

`gh api` against the job's log refuses as soon as its output is not a terminal. It prints this, and writes nothing to the file or the pipe you gave it:

```text
the response contains terminal escape sequences; pass --allow-escape-sequences to output it anyway
```

Piped to `grep`, the call finds no match, which reads as a log with no error in it.
sections.Environment: The `gh` CLI, seen on 2.100.0, reading a job of `.github/workflows/kac.yml` on this repository. The job's log contains ANSI colour codes.
sections.Cause: `gh run view` fetches logs for a whole run, so it waits until every job has finished. `gh api` reads one job's log straight away. It refuses to print terminal escape sequences unless you pass `--allow-escape-sequences`. The refusal goes to standard error, so a file or a pipe receives no log.
sections.Resolution:
1. Read the job id from the check's URL, which `gh pr checks <pr>` prints. It is the number after `/job/`.
2. Fetch that job's log with `gh api`, allow the escape sequences, and strip them with `sed`:

   ```sh
   gh api --allow-escape-sequences repos/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/actions/jobs/<job-id>/logs \
     | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | cut -c30-
   ```

   `cut -c30-` drops the timestamp at the head of each line.

3. Add `| grep -n '##\[error\]'` to go straight to the error line.

The command prints the log as plain text, and `grep -c $'\x1b'` over its output counts no escape byte. It works while the rest of the run is still in progress.
sections.Why it happens: `gh` guards a terminal against escape sequences an API response could carry, and treats a job log as one of those responses. `gh run view` has no `--allow-escape-sequences` flag, so only `gh api` can pass the guard.
